_meta.description: Four south-polar notional sites from NASA 2020 ISRU study, slide 6. NASA LOLA elevation, derived slope/local horizon, JPL Horizons sunlight. No guaranteed ice deposit.
_meta.freeze_scope: Preserve coordinates and provenance; regenerate with tools/prepare_polar_data.py.

sites.name: Connecting Ridge (Study Site 001)
sites.description: Artemis 001: notional south-polar location in NASA’s 2020 ISRU case study. Not an approved landing pad. Nearby shadowed terrain motivates prospecting; recoverable ice is unconfirmed.

coordinates.source: NASA GRC/JSC Kleinhenz & Paz (2020), Case Study for Lunar ISRU Systems Utilizing Polar Water, slide 6, Artemis 001. https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20205008303/downloads/AIAA_ASCEND2020_Kleinhenz_presentation_final.pdf

illumination_pct.source: NASA/JPL Horizons DE441 Sun/Earth geometry plus NASA LOLA-derived local horizon; 2026-10-19 through 2026-11-18 UTC, 15-minute quadrature. Mean visible fraction of the solar disk, including Earth occultation; not a measured NASA illumination percentage. Regional horizon coverage excludes more distant terrain. Power additionally accounts for solar distance.

elevation_m.source: NASA LRO LOLA / Barker et al. 2021, PGDA product 78; Site01 and Site04 5-m DEMs, USGS COG distribution. https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78
elevation_m.sample_method: Bilinear interpolation at published study coordinate; south polar stereographic, lon_0=0, lat_0=-90, R=1737400 m

slope_deg.source: NASA LRO LOLA / Barker et al. 2021, PGDA product 78; Site01 and Site04 5-m DEMs, USGS COG distribution. https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/products/78
slope_deg.sample_method: Central elevation differences over 10-m baseline; derived slope, not a sampled slope product

hydrogen_ppm.source: A notional ISRU study site is not evidence of an extractable deposit. Local sampling and confirmation are required.

horizon.method: Derived local horizon from 10-m sampled DEM, curvature included; maximum per 0.5-degree azimuth bin. Zero-degree floor. Distant terrain beyond regional coverage and DEM uncertainties omitted; not a mission-grade illumination forecast.
